title: Declare the existing Homebrew baseline in nix-darwin
description: Add a Darwin Homebrew module that declares the currently required taps, requested formulae, and all 15 casks. Do not migrate or uninstall tools in this step. Keep onActivation.autoUpdate and upgrade conservative and cleanup disabled so the first activation is additive and reversible. Remove only taps proven unused by the declared inventory.
acceptance_criteria: darwin-rebuild build succeeds; activating produces no unintended removals; all current casks and required custom formulae remain installed; and brew bundle check reports the declared baseline satisfied.
notes:
Implemented review candidate: added modules/darwin/homebrew.nix and imported it from hosts/macbook-pro/default.nix. Declares 57 requested brews, all 15 casks, and 7 taps proven required by declared custom packages. Keeps autoUpdate=false, upgrade=false, cleanup=none. Custom Homebrew 6 trust declarations use homebrew.extraConfig because nix-darwin 25.11 lacks typed trusted fields. Safe validation passed: nix flake check path:/Users/scaf/.config/nix-conf --all-systems --no-build; full Darwin system build with --no-link; generated Brewfile inventory parity (57 brews/15 casks); HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1 brew bundle check --no-upgrade reports dependencies satisfied; git diff --check. No activation, uninstall, cleanup, commit, push, or bead close performed pending review.
Review follow-up: alphabetized all 51 typed brew entries. Verified they are unique and sorted; flake check and git diff --check still pass. No activation or closure performed.
Completion attempt: final Darwin build after ordering fix passed. System activation is blocked because non-interactive sudo reports 'a password is required'. Human must run: sudo darwin-rebuild switch --flake 'path:/Users/scaf/.config/nix-conf#macbook-pro'. Keep bead in_progress until post-activation package/service checks pass. The two-axis code review already completed with no hard standards violations or confirmed spec defects; only activation-dependent acceptance remains.
Post-activation verification passed: /run/current-system exactly matches the expected built path; Homebrew inventory remains 235 formulae and 15 casks; generated Brewfile bundle check passes; yabai and skhd are running with last exit code 0. Final two-axis review: no blocking standards findings and spec acceptance MET.
close_reason: Implemented declarative Homebrew baseline, activated successfully, verified no package removals, passed bundle check and service checks, and completed final two-axis review.

title: Capture and classify the current Homebrew inventory
description: Record the migration baseline and classify requested packages by destination. Observed inventory: 235 formulae, 53 requested leaves, 15 casks, 12 taps, no pinned formulae, and five installed-but-inactive service definitions (dolt, herdr, php, php@8.2, unbound). The Brewfile additionally records uv tool browser-use and npm globals @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, @modelcontextprotocol/server-github, 9router, better-sqlite3, oh-my-claude-sisyphus, sql.js, systray2, and yaml-language-server. A nixpkgs availability probe found direct aarch64-darwin candidates for most standard CLIs; exceptions or uncertain identities include beads, beads_viewer, composer, firefoxpwa, flux9s, herdr, hunk, rtk, plannotator-tui, floci, and the custom omp/mole formulae.
acceptance_criteria: Counts, taps, casks, requested formulae, language-global packages, service state, and initial Nix availability are documented in this issue and can be used as the baseline for later phases.
close_reason: Inventory captured from brew leaves, brew bundle dump, taps, services, and nixpkgs aarch64-darwin availability checks.

title: Migrate Homebrew to declarative Nix management
description: Gradually make the Mac software inventory reproducible through nix-darwin and Home Manager without a disruptive one-shot migration. Current baseline: 235 installed formulae (53 leaves), 15 casks, 12 taps, no pinned formulae, and no active Homebrew services. The generated Brewfile also contains one uv tool and eight global npm packages. Preserve working tools first, move portable CLI tools to Nix in tested batches, keep macOS-native applications and unsupported/custom formulae in declarative Homebrew, then enable cleanup only after parity is verified.
design: Use nix-darwin homebrew.* as the declarative bridge. Start with cleanup disabled. Migrate one category at a time; for each package verify binary identity, version expectations, config/data paths, shell integration, and a representative command before uninstalling the Homebrew copy. Prefer Home Manager for user CLI tools, nix-darwin for machine services/system tools, and project devShells for project-specific runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: All intentionally installed brews, casks, taps, npm globals, and uv tools have an explicit owner: Nix/Home Manager, declarative Homebrew, project environment, or documented exception. A rebuild succeeds, daily tools are smoke-tested, stale dependencies/taps are removed, and bootstrap documentation matches the final configuration.

title: Evaluate custom-tap and fast-moving tools
description:
## Goal
Check package identity, release freshness, and Darwin behavior for beads, beads_viewer, opencode, omp, flux9s, floci, herdr, hunk, mole, rtk, and plannotator-tui. Select declarative Homebrew or a maintained Nix package for each.

## Method
Compare the installed formula upstream and version with nixpkgs. Treat same-name packages as unverified until their upstream identity matches. Prefer existing trusted taps initially; only add an overlay when its maintenance burden is justified.

## Findings
Initial probing found direct nixpkgs candidates for opencode and a package named mole, but identity/version parity remains unverified. Direct aarch64-darwin candidates were not found for beads, beads_viewer, flux9s, herdr, hunk, rtk, plannotator-tui, floci, or the custom omp formula. Record final findings here during the spike.
acceptance_criteria: Every custom tool has a verified upstream identity and selected source. Unused taps are identified. Any proposed Nix package includes an update-maintenance plan; otherwise the tool remains explicitly declared in Homebrew.

title: Migrate cloud, infrastructure, and developer CLIs
description: Evaluate and migrate standard development tools with direct nixpkgs candidates: ansible, awscli2, azure-cli, biome, fluxcd, gemini-cli, graphviz, imagemagick, k6, and related Kubernetes tooling. Check plugins, credential discovery, completions, and version requirements before changing ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Chosen tools are Nix-managed, authentication/config paths still work, completions are available where expected, representative workflows pass, and removed Homebrew entries have no dependent requested formulae that still require them.

title: Choose a policy for language runtimes and global packages
description:
## Decision
Choose ownership for node, pnpm, yarn, global npm packages, Python 3.11/3.12, pyenv, pipx, PHP 8.2, composer, dotnet-sdk@8, browser-use installed through uv, and gcloud-cli.

## Rationale
Language runtimes and mutable global package ecosystems have different reproducibility and update needs from ordinary CLI tools. Blindly replacing them can break projects or remove globally installed agent tooling.

## Alternatives Considered
Home Manager packages; per-project devShells; language version managers; declarative Homebrew; or a documented hybrid. Compare version pinning, project compatibility, global tool packaging, upgrade cadence, and work-laptop portability before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A documented per-runtime decision identifies the owner, required versions, global tools to package or retain, project-local strategy, migration order, and rollback method. Follow-up implementation beads exist for decisions too large for one change.

title: Migrate low-risk portable CLI tools to Home Manager
description: Move a first small batch of portable user tools from Homebrew to Home Manager, then remove those entries from homebrew.brews. Initial candidates: actionlint, age, eza, fd, fzf, gh, lazygit, ripgrep, sops, kubectx, kubernetes-helm, and mkcert. Handle shell integrations through Home Manager rather than Homebrew-sourced scripts. Keep batches small enough to identify regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Each selected command resolves to /nix/store or the Home Manager profile, representative commands work, shell startup is clean, darwin-rebuild succeeds, and the corresponding Homebrew formulae are no longer requested.

title: Validate reproducible Mac bootstrap and documentation
description: Verify the final repository can provision the intended Nix/Home Manager/Homebrew state from a clean or isolated test context. Update README commands, prerequisites, work-laptop limitations, secret restoration, and manual post-install steps.
acceptance_criteria: flake check and darwin build pass; documented bootstrap commands match the flake output; all intentionally managed software is represented; secrets are excluded; and remaining manual steps are explicit.

title: Enable Homebrew cleanup after migration parity
description: After all migration categories are resolved, review brew leaves, autoremove candidates, taps, services, and casks. Change nix-darwin Homebrew activation cleanup from none to the agreed mode only after a dry run and rollback review. Do not remove application data or credentials.
acceptance_criteria: All remaining Homebrew entries are intentional and declared, stale taps/dependencies are removed, brew doctor has no migration-caused failures, cleanup is safely enabled or explicitly deferred, and a rollback generation is known.

title: Migrate media, networking, and native utility formulae
description: Evaluate the remaining standard formulae such as arping, ffmpeg, ghostscript, mpv, neovim, nmap, nss, sshpass, terminal-notifier, tree-sitter, tree-sitter-cli, wireguard-tools, and xorriso. Verify macOS integrations, codecs, plugins, and runtime behavior; leave a formula in Homebrew if the Nix build is materially less functional.
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate has a tested destination, selected Nix-managed tools work for actual use cases, retained Homebrew exceptions are documented, and Neovim migration does not overwrite the existing dirty ~/.config/nvim repository.
